title: Wire RewardConfigController's async mutations to the RewardForm.loading/.error fields the screen already renders
why: RewardForm carries loading/error fields and reward_configuration_screen.dart fully renders them (full-screen CircularProgressIndicator for form.loading, a dedicated error Scaffold for form.error) — but grep-confirmed, the controller's 4 async mutation methods (saveReward, toggleEnabled, deleteMilestone, milestonesForCurrentLadder) never set either field to a non-default value anywhere in the file; only bootstrap() touches them, always resetting to false/null. The screen's own try/catch only catches TutorWriteException per call site (for the tutor-permission-denied case). Any OTHER DB failure during a save/toggle/delete (constraint violation, disk error) is an unhandled Future rejection: the user taps Save, sees no spinner (loading never flips true) and no error (error never gets set) — the operation silently fails with zero feedback, while the fully-built error UI remains permanently dead code.
recommendation: In each of the 4 mutation methods, set `state = state.copyWith(loading: true)` before the DB call and wrap it in try/catch: on success `loading:false`; on any exception (not just TutorWriteException) `state.copyWith(loading:false, error: <mapped message>)`, or migrate the class to expose `AsyncValue<RewardForm>`-style guard semantics.
acceptance_criteria: saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/milestonesForCurrentLadder each leave state.error non-null (not an unhandled Future rejection) when the underlying DB call throws anything other than TutorWriteException.
Widget test: a fake RewardMilestoneService/DB that throws a generic exception from upsertMilestone; assert the screen renders the form.error branch instead of hanging or throwing past the test.

Rule-0 checker: a grep/lint that flags a state class with loading/error-shaped fields where the owning @riverpod class file contains zero `state.copyWith(error:` (or equivalent) assignment with a non-null literal — i.e., a 'declared-but-dead error field' detector.

refutations: Evidence checks out (grep-verified: none of saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/milestonesForCurrentLadder ever set loading/error; screen catches only TutorWriteException at 3 call sites). But this duplicates an already-filed, UPHELD main-sweep finding: verified-findings-r3.json 'Delete or wire
corrections: No factual error in the cited evidence — form.loading/form.error are confirmed dead (only bootstrap() touches them) and the 4 async mutations are confirmed to lack try/catch beyond the screen's TutorWriteException-only wrappers. The defect is real; the problem is novelty/duplication and severity calibration relative to the already-filed twin P3 finding, not correctness of the grep evidence.

Site count should be 3 real mutation methods (saveReward, toggleEnabled, deleteMilestone), not 4 — milestonesForCurrentLadder is a read-only query consumed by a separate widget-local FutureBuilder and structurally cannot/should not be wired to form.loading/form.error without causing a UX regression (whole-form spinner over a small list refresh). The recommendation's primary fix (manual try/catch assigning state) contradicts the literal SM-5 text cited as the rule; genuine SM-5 compliance requires migrating to AsyncValue<RewardForm>, offered only as a secondary 'or' in the recommendation.

Two corrections: (1) Rule fit is weak — SM-5 mandates AsyncValue.guard and explicitly forbids "hand-manage loading/error with a try/catch that assigns state," yet the finding's own primary recommended fix (wrap each method in try/catch, `state.copyWith(loading:..., error:...)`) is exactly that forbidden pattern; EH-2 ("no raw exception reaches presentation") fits the actual defect better than SM-5. (2) "sites: 4" overcounts: milestonesForCurrentLadder is a pure read consumed via independent FutureBuilder (manage_rewards_list.dart / _InlineRewardsSection), never wired to RewardForm.loading/error by design — only saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone are genuine instances of the described root cause (3 sites, not 4). Also "constraint violation" is misleading — RewardMilestoneService persists via SharedPreferences, not SQL; the real failure surface is the Firestore push inside _persistAndSync.
